children: A team of engineering students from Sona College of Technology, Salem has won the MECA Global Finals 2026, a factory automation contest organised by Mitsubishi Electric, held in Tokyo.
The Indian team emerged as the overall winner after competing against national teams from Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand.

The four-member team comprising Tharanika K, Seralathan R, Vijay B and Tharana A S had earlier emerged as the winner of the 6th Mitsubishi Electric Cup National Level Competition held in Pune in February 2026.
They presented an intelligent Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) programming assistant designed for Mitsubishi Electric’s automation systems.
The solution allows engineers to describe a machine’s intended behaviour in simple English, which the AI then converts into industrial PLC code.

This can eliminate manual coding that requires specialised increased technical expertise, reducing development time and making errors easy to identify and rectify, particularly during machine commissioning.

“Sona College team built a tool that lets an engineer describe a factory machine’s behaviour in simple English, and AI turns that description into working PLC code. The prototype won the approval of the jury and passed the rigours of jury questions,” Chocko Valliappa, Vice Chairman, Sona Institutions.

title: Team from Sona College of Technology wins factory automation contest in Tokyo
